title: House subcommittee discusses NLIC, nuclear spent fuel policy
summary: Six states—Idaho, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Utah, and West Virginia—have now signed memorandums of understanding as finalists for the Department of Energy’s Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses (NLIC) program. Some or all of these states could very well host a facility or facilities to handle multiple stages of the nuclear fuel cycle, including enrichment, fabrication, recycling, reprocessing, and disposal.

title: We’ve crossed the nuclear tipping point
summary: Bahran Twenty years ago, I walked across a graduation stage with a nuclear engineering degree and a promise that the nuclear renaissance was coming. It never came. The hard part was not the physics. Fermi demonstrated the technical viability of fission as an energy source in 1942, achieving the first man-made criticality with a pile of uranium and graphite bricks under a Chicago stadium. The hard part was everything wrapped around the physics, and that’s the part that has just changed, with three shifts lining up at the same time.

title: Nusano releases Launch Pad enrichment project details
summary: At the end of August, Utah-based company Nusano was chosen as one of the second-round selections by the National Reactor Innovation Center for a project through its Nuclear Energy Launch Pad. Yesterday, the company announced the details of that project, which will focus on high-assay low-enrichment uranium production. This turn to enrichment comes as the company continues to develop a radioisotope production facility in Utah.
